title: The minimum overlap problem for three parts
statement: Split [0,3] into three parts of equal measure, allowing fractional membership: measurable f_1, f_2, f_3: [0,3] -> [0,1] with f_1 + f_2 + f_3 = 1 and the integral of each f_a equal to 1. The overlap of parts a != b at shift x is the integral of f_a(t) f_b(t - x) dt (the continuous count of differences x between part a and part b). Let mu_3 be the infimum, over all such splittings, of the largest overlap over all pairs a != b and shifts x. Determine mu_3. This is the three-part version of Erdos's minimum overlap problem (two parts of {1, ..., 2n}, constant mu = 0.380...). Known: 1/6 <= mu_3 <= 56061/200000 = 0.280305; find a splitting with a smaller largest overlap.
submission: Text file: 60 lines of three integers between 0 and 600, the values of f_1, f_2, f_3 (times 600) on the 60 cells of width 1/20 of [0,3]; each line must sum to 600 and each column to 12000. Other grids and denominators can be checked with the checker's M and DEN arguments.
score: the largest overlap of the step functions, an exact rational number (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026: a 60-cell step splitting found by multiplicative gradient steps on a smoothed maximum with Sinkhorn rebalancing (tools/overlap3.py), rounded to multiples of 1/600

context: Erdos's minimum overlap problem (1955) asks how evenly {1, ..., 2n} can be split into two halves so that no difference occurs too often between them; the limiting constant mu lies between White's lower bound 0.379005 (arXiv:2201.05704) and the best constructions near 0.38086, and it is constant 1b of the optimization-constants repository. With three parts every pair of parts must avoid every shift at once. Two elementary bounds frame mu_3: averaging over shifts gives at least 1/6 for each pair (the overlaps of a pair integrate to 1 over shifts in [-3, 3]), and the uniform splitting f_a = 1/3 gives 1/3; our step functions reach 0.2803, so non-uniform splittings help, but how far is open.
references: P. Erdos, Some remarks on number theory, Riveon Lematematika 9 (1955) 45-48
J. K. Haugland, The minimum overlap problem revisited, arXiv:1609.08000
E. P. White, Erdos' minimum overlap problem, arXiv:2201.05704
Optimization constants in mathematics, constant 1b (github.com/teorth/optimizationproblems), read 9 November 2026

novelty.verdict: new. No version of Erdos's minimum overlap problem with three or more parts was found (arXiv, web search); the two-part problem and its continuous form are the closest.
closest: Erdos's two-part minimum overlap problem (constant mu, repository constant 1b); the three-part constant is a different quantity.
novelty.benchmark: no entry; the benchmark's one-dimensional constants are 1a, 1c and 1d

rows: 0.28062 (float; the optimizer did not improve on 60 cells)
first_values.note: Upper bounds; the uniform splitting gives 1/3 and the averaging bound is 1/6.

baseline.text: 56061/200000 = 0.280305 (60-cell splitting in `refs/overlap-three.txt`), held by Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 9 November 2026. Lower bound 1/6 by averaging the overlaps of one pair over all shifts.

bound.source: the overlaps of a pair integrate to 1 over shifts in [-3, 3]
